title: Capstone Reporting: Sales, Products and Customers
learningObjectives: Join related sales entities to produce useful reports.
Calculate product revenue from quantity and sale-time price.
Use GROUP BY to define the report's aggregation level.
Use HAVING to filter groups by aggregated values.
Rank report results with a window function.

understand.concept: A useful sales database supports reports across related tables. Joins combine customer, order and product details; aggregates calculate totals; GROUP BY creates summaries; HAVING filters groups after aggregation.
understand.whyItMatters: Reporting queries turn operational records into information about sales, popular products and customer activity.
understand.analogy: A database capstone is like a complete shop workflow: records, rules, operations and reports must all work together.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy does not model database isolation, concurrent workloads, deployment security or recovery guarantees.

explain.narrative:
## Reporting model
Join order headers to customers and order items, then join products for names and categories. Use stable keys for relationships and avoid joining on display text.

## Aggregates
SUM(quantity * unit_price) calculates sales value. COUNT(DISTINCT order_id) counts unique orders. GROUP BY defines the reporting grain, such as one row per product or category.

## HAVING and ranking
Use WHERE to filter source rows before grouping and HAVING to filter aggregated groups. Window functions can rank products by revenue while preserving one row per product.

examples.title: Create a reporting sales table
examples.code: CREATE TABLE cap19_report_sales (sale_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, customer TEXT NOT NULL, product TEXT NOT NULL, category TEXT NOT NULL, quantity INTEGER NOT NULL, unit_price INTEGER NOT NULL);
examples.explanation: This example demonstrates create a reporting sales table in the CodeSaathi inventory-and-sales capstone. Verify the data and business rule.

examples.title: Insert report rows
examples.explanation: This example demonstrates insert report rows in the CodeSaathi inventory-and-sales capstone. Verify the data and business rule.

examples.title: Calculate revenue by product
examples.code: SELECT product, SUM(quantity * unit_price) AS revenue FROM cap19_report_sales GROUP BY product ORDER BY revenue DESC, product;
examples.explanation: This example demonstrates calculate revenue by product in the CodeSaathi inventory-and-sales capstone. Verify the data and business rule.

examples.title: Filter categories by total revenue
examples.code: SELECT category, SUM(quantity * unit_price) AS revenue FROM cap19_report_sales GROUP BY category HAVING SUM(quantity * unit_price) >= 500 ORDER BY revenue DESC;
examples.explanation: This example demonstrates filter categories by total revenue in the CodeSaathi inventory-and-sales capstone. Verify the data and business rule.

examples.title: Rank products by revenue
examples.code: WITH product_totals AS (SELECT product, SUM(quantity * unit_price) AS revenue FROM cap19_report_sales GROUP BY product) SELECT product, revenue, DENSE_RANK() OVER (ORDER BY revenue DESC) AS revenue_rank FROM product_totals ORDER BY revenue_rank, product;
examples.explanation: This example demonstrates rank products by revenue in the CodeSaathi inventory-and-sales capstone. Verify the data and business rule.

practise.guidedTask: Run the examples and explain why Cable has the highest revenue even though Case has a higher unit price.
practise.independentTask: Build a report that shows revenue by customer and category, filters groups with HAVING and ranks the top three products by revenue.
hints: Calculate line revenue as quantity multiplied by unit_price.
